diet.note: Gallimimus had a toothless beak, and its diet is disputed. NHM lists it as omnivorous and PBDB as herbivore or omnivore; Zanno & Makovicky 2011 infer herbivory for ornithomimosaurs from skull features; Norell et al. 2001 suggested that ornithomimids with preserved beak tissue strained food from sediment in water.

timeRange.note: PBDB dates G. bullatus occurrences (Nemegt Formation, Mongolia) to the Maastrichtian; the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 Maastrichtian stage boundaries. The Nemegt Formation is not precisely dated (Zanno & Makovicky 2013 cite about 69 and 68 Ma). Genus-level PBDB records from the Baruungoyot Formation and Uzbekistan are not used.

massKg.note: Single published estimate (NHM Dino Directory); method not stated.

summary.en: Gallimimus was an 'ostrich dinosaur' from Mongolia, living near the very end of the Age of Dinosaurs. About 6 metres long, it was a fast runner with a toothless beak. Its name means 'chicken mimic' because its neck bones resemble a chicken's. Nobody is sure what it ate: plants, small animals, or food strained from water.

text.en: Experts estimate that Gallimimus could run at 47 to 55 kilometres per hour, more than twice as fast as a fit human.

uncertain.note: Herbivory, omnivory and filter-feeding have all been proposed for ornithomimids (NHM; Zanno & Makovicky 2011; Norell et al. 2001).
